summary: Results of a Dexcom-funded study published in the New England Journal of Medicine Wednesday demonstrated that people with Type 2 diabetes who don’t take insulin may benefit from wearing a continuous glucose monitor. Dexcom first shared the results at the American Diabetes Association’s Scientific Sessions this summer. The study found that people who wore a CGM had a larger reduction in hemoglobin A1c than people who received routine care after 26 weeks. The published results come as diabetes tech firms anticipate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to expand Medicare coverage of CGMs for people with diabetes who don’t take insulin. Having a peer-reviewed publication in a leading medical journal “should be a catalyst” for a CMS decision, William Blair analysts wrote in a research note.
title: NEJM study supports CGM use for people with diabetes who don’t take insulin

summary: Zimmer Biomet said Tuesday it has inked a multi-year extension to its exclusive distribution agreement with Think Surgical. The deal, which extends an agreement signed in 2024, positions Zimmer to continue distributing an exclusive version of Think’s TMINI wireless handheld miniature robotic system. Zimmer’s exclusive version of TMINI is compatible with its Persona knee system, a personalized product used in total knee replacements.
title: Zimmer and Think Surgical pen multi-year extension to robotic surgery deal

summary: Siemens Healthineers said Monday that it will no longer sell general imaging ultrasound systems, focusing instead on ultrasound used in procedural imaging. The company will focus on systems used in interventional cardiology and electrophysiology procedures. Siemens Healthineers said this approach will allow it to bring together its imaging systems, software capabilities and partnerships with heart device companies to support physicians in increasingly complex procedures. Siemens Healthineers said it will continue to provide support for its general ultrasound systems, including maintenance, software updates and transducer availability.
title: Siemens Healthineers to stop selling general ultrasound systems

summary: The payments were made after a California arbitrator found private text messages between Orthofix executives couldn’t be considered cause for firing.
title: Orthofix pays former executives $24M in damages

summary: Agilent said Tuesday that it has agreed to buy digital pathology software provider Proscia for $240 million upfront. The deal, which includes up to $30 million in milestones, will give Agilent control of technology that connects slide scanners, laboratory information systems and other parts of the pathology workflow. Agilent’s deal comes months after Roche agreed to buy PathAI for up to $1.05 billion. Evercore ISI analysts noted that Agilent “got the rights to play in this market at a lower price point.”
title: Agilent to buy Proscia for $240M

summary: For the second straight quarter, the cardiovascular unit experienced slower sales growth due to ongoing struggles in the Abiomed business.
title: J&J’s medtech business slows again in Q3

summary: Steris said Monday it struck a $2.1 billion deal to acquire Xodus Medical for its portfolio of consumable healthcare products. Xodus’ portfolio includes Pink Pad patient-positioning products and the See Sharp laparoscopic cleaning and defogging device. The company expects annual sales to hit $245 million this year. Buying Xodus “makes sense” for Steris because it expands the company’s healthcare consumables offering with high-growth, high-margin products, Needham analysts said in a note to investors.
title: Steris inks $2.1B Xodus buyout to expand consumables portfolio

summary: Ascensia Diabetes Care led a $36 million Series B round in London-based glucose sensor maker Sava Technologies, the startup said Friday. The companies also struck a strategic partnership that gives Ascensia exclusive commercialization and distribution rights, starting in Europe. Based in Basel, Switzerland, Ascensia is a subsidiary of Tokyo’s PHC Holdings. Sava is developing a wearable glucose sensor that could expand to other biomarkers in the future. Sava hopes for the device to provide more options for people who use continuous glucose monitors in a market currently dominated by Abbott and Dexcom.
title: Ascensia leads $36M funding round for glucose sensor startup

summary: Stryker said Monday it has partnered with soft tissue robotics firm CMR Surgical, investing about $400 million into the company and becoming the exclusive U.S. distributor of CMR’s system. Cambridge, England-based CMR received Food and Drug Administration clearance for its latest robotic system last year to perform gallbladder procedures in the U.S. As of early 2026, the company had performed more than 45,000 procedures globally, J.P. Morgan analyst Robbie Marcus wrote in a research note. Stryker had been expected to enter the soft tissue robotics market for years, Stifel analyst Rick Wise wrote in a research note. With competitors Johnson & Johnson and Medtronic receiving FDA nods for their own robots in the U.S., Wise added, “it feels like a now or never moment for Stryker to make the decision.”
title: Stryker enters soft tissue robotics with $400M investment in CMR Surgical

summary: Philips is updating instructions for an ultrasound system after reporting eight serious injuries and four deaths, the Food and Drug Administration said Friday. The FDA, which published an early alert about Philips’ actions, said the software issue can delay the use of the portable Lumify diagnostic ultrasound system. Philips wrote to customers about the issue last month, recommending actions to mitigate the risks while it develops a software update to fix the problem.
title: Philips updates instructions for ultrasound system linked to 4 deaths
